title: Physics · Paper 2 (HL) — original full-format practice
subject: physics
instructions: Answer every question using the response area attached to it. An approved calculator is required. Use the original reference data supplied within this sample; no external data booklet is needed. Show calculations, units, diagrams and reasoning where required. No separate answer sheet is used.

resources.label: Original induction investigation
resources.text: A coil of 250 turns and area 3.2 × 10⁻³ m² is perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field. The field falls linearly from 0.80 T to 0.20 T in 0.15 s. The coil resistance is 4.0 Ω.

resources.label: Reference data for this sample
resources.text:
g = 9.81 m s⁻²
G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²
Speed of light c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹
Elementary charge e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C

questions.label: Question 1 — electromagnetic induction
questions.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the average induced emf and current. State the direction principle used to determine the induced current.

questions.label: Question 2 — fields
questions.prompt: A satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius 7.2 × 10⁶ m around a planet of mass 6.0 × 10²⁴ kg. Calculate its orbital speed and period. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².

questions.label: Question 3 — quantum physics
questions.prompt: Explain why the photoelectric effect supports a particulate model of electromagnetic radiation. Refer to threshold frequency and intensity.

questions.label: Question 4 — thermal physics
questions.prompt: A student claims that temperature measures the total energy stored in an object. Evaluate the claim using microscopic models and two contrasting examples.

questions.label: Question 5 — mechanics
questions.prompt: A trolley moves down an incline with a resistive force proportional to speed. Derive the terminal speed, sketch speed against time, and use supplied measurements to estimate the proportionality constant.

questions.label: Question 6 — oscillations
questions.prompt: A mass–spring system has amplitude 0.080 m and period 1.60 s. Determine its angular frequency, maximum speed and maximum acceleration, then calculate the speed at displacement 0.050 m.

questions.label: Question 7 — wave behaviour
questions.prompt: Two coherent sources produce an interference pattern. Use path difference to locate maxima, calculate fringe separation for a double slit, and explain the effect of increasing slit separation.

questions.label: Question 8 — electric fields
questions.prompt: An electron is accelerated through a potential difference and enters a uniform electric field. Calculate its speed, subsequent acceleration and deflection, stating the assumptions used.

questions.label: Question 9 — nuclear physics
questions.prompt: Use mass data to calculate the binding energy per nucleon of a nucleus. Compare it with two neighbouring nuclei and explain what the comparison suggests about possible energy-releasing reactions.

questions.label: Question 10 — energy and climate
questions.prompt: Evaluate a simplified planetary energy-balance model. Explain albedo and emissivity, calculate an equilibrium temperature from supplied values, and discuss two limitations of the model.
